about.title: Ukiah Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When someone dies because another person or company was careless, California law gives the family a way to seek accountability in civil court. In Ukiah, that might follow a collision on N State Street or Talmage Road, a fall at a business near Airport Park Boulevard, a medical error, or an incident on a job site. The most recent final year on record, 2025, shows 48 injury collisions and 53 people hurt in the city, with no traffic deaths counted. Fatal losses here are uncommon, which can leave a grieving family feeling isolated when one does happen. The law limits who may file: a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, then certain dependents and heirs. Two years from the date of death is the general deadline, and it shrinks when a public agency is involved. We handle wrongful death claims on contingency in Mendocino County, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. Our team can sort out who in your family may bring the claim.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general limit is two years from the date of death, and claims against a city, county, or state agency carry a much shorter window. Reaching out sooner protects those options.

items.title: A separate civil path
items.desc: A wrongful death case is independent of any criminal proceeding and can seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Our team works on contingency.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on S State Street in Ukiah. Do we need to wait for the criminal case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves separately from any charges the district attorney may bring. The two-year deadline runs from the date of death regardless of the criminal timeline, so it makes sense to talk with us early. Our team can also gather collision records while they are still readily available.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children have the first right to file. If there are none, certain dependents and heirs may qualify. The rules can get complicated with blended families or estranged relatives, which is one reason to have an attorney review your situation.

items.question: What does it cost to contact you?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free case review and handle wrongful death claims on contingency, meaning we are paid only if there is a recovery.
